story: Sunny and 84 degrees on Magnolia Loop, Gary is hopeful as he pulls his newly lit golf cart up beside Rosa and offers to wire up anything she needs for the parade. Donna, looking determined, is tucking the extra pink flamingos behind a hedge so that only three stand in view from the street. Hal, watching closely through his binoculars, is counting how many flamingos he can still see, while Rosa, cheerful as ever, invites everyone to her porch for hot coffee and a talk about the Halloween decor deadline.
events: Donna (donna flamingo flock): Pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving exactly three visible from the street
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Raise binoculars and count how many flamingos are visible from the street

gary.thought_process: I just rolled out onto Magnolia Loop with the cart fully rigged: lights, speakers, brackets, all tested in the garage. That's exactly the kind of exterior modification L-01 says needs Architectural Review, and I never filed anything. The memories say the parade is rolling and the costume contest is starting at the Town Square, but it's already Sunday, November 1 and the parade seems to be over. Either way, I want folks to enjoy the rig, and I want to feel useful. Rosa just showed up and promised treats and a warm porch, so a friendly word to her is the natural move. Don't blast the speakers, though. Better to keep things neighborly and ask whether she needs anything fixed or rigged for the parade.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Rosa! Cart's all rigged up with lights and speakers, finally. If you've got anything that needs fixing or wiring for the parade, you just say the word.

donna.thought_process: Hal is standing right here waiting on my promise. I told him I was moving the extras behind the hedge, so the honest thing is to actually do it now. Interacting with the flamingo flock to thin it to three keeps my word and satisfies L-02. Gary just arrived too, so I can pitch pickleball after the lawn is squared away.

parameters.content: Pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving exactly three visible from the street

hal.thought_process: Donna says she's moving the extras behind the hedge and keeping three out front. That's what L-02 requires, but I count with my own eyes, not on promises. The flock is right here to inspect. Gary and Rosa just walked up, and I've gone soft on both of them lately, so the cart notebook can wait one more day. Best move is to check the flamingo flock and tally what's visible from the street.

parameters.content: Raise binoculars and count how many flamingos are visible from the street

rosa.thought_process: I just stepped out onto Magnolia Loop and all three neighbors are here at once, which is exactly what I've been working toward with the dinner and the porch coffee. I was planning to mention the November 7 Halloween decor deadline without sounding like the HOA. Hal is supposed to come to my porch for coffee, so I should greet the group warmly and tie it all together. Gary arrived just before me, so nobody has said anything yet. Best to start with Hal since he's the one I'm expecting, keep it light, and invite everyone toward the porch instead of lecturing in the street.

parameters.content: Hal, there you are! Coffee's hot on my porch, and Gary and Donna are welcome too. I want to talk through the Halloween decor deadline together before anybody's flamingos get dressed up.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
